title: A population code for semantics in human hippocampus
title_zh: 人类海马体语义分布编码
abstract: Motivated by the successes of large language models (LLMs), we hypothesized that semantic information in the brain may be expressed in distributed patterns of neural activity. We recorded responses of hippocampal neurons while individuals listened to narrative speech. Here, using an encoding model approach, we find robust encoding of semantics, even after controlling for phonemics and grammar. Individual words had complex selectivities that included multiple words in multiple semantic categories. Similar to embedding vectors in LLMs, distance between neural population responses correlated with semantic distance. For semantically similar words, even contextual embedders showed an inverse correlation between semantic and neural distances; we attribute this pattern to the noise-mitigating benefits of contrastive coding. Finally, neural population activity aligned most closely with GPT-2 embeddings, and variation in response patterns correlated with LLM-derived polysemy measures, indicating that semantic encoding is largely contextualized. Ultimately, these results provide a neurocomputational account for understanding how hippocampal neurons encode word meaning during language listening.
abstract_zh: 受大型语言模型（LLMs）成功的启发，我们假设大脑中的语义信息可能以分布式神经活动模式的形式表达。我们在个体聆听叙事语言时记录了海马神经元的反应。在此，利用编码模型方法，我们发现即使在控制音位和语法后，语义信息也能得到稳健编码。个别词汇具有复杂的选择性，包括多个语义类别中的多个词汇。类似于LLMs中的嵌入向量，神经群体反应之间的距离与语义距离相关。对于语义相似的词汇，即使是上下文嵌入器也表现出语义距离与神经距离之间的反相关；我们将此模式归因于对比编码的降噪益处。最后，神经群体活动与GPT-2嵌入最为一致，且反应模式的变异与LLM派生的多义性度量相关，表明语义编码主要是语境化的。最终，这些结果为理解海马神经元在语言聆听过程中编码词义提供了神经计算账户。
